title: JavaScript files are included but not type-checked, creating a silent quality gap

evidence.quote: No "checkJs" option is set anywhere in this config

reasoning: With `allowJs: true`, `.js` files participate in the program, but without `checkJs: true` they are not type-checked. This creates an inconsistent contract where TypeScript files are strict but JavaScript can carry unchecked API/shape errors into runtime and releases.
recommendation: Either disable JavaScript ingestion (`allowJs: false`) or enforce checking for JS (`checkJs: true`). If migration is in progress, scope JS inclusion narrowly and enable `checkJs` per folder via layered tsconfig files.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were provided for this feature, and this is a compile-time configuration gap that runtime tests may not deterministically detect.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI typecheck step (`tsc --noEmit`) with a fixture `.js` file containing an obvious type misuse; verify the build fails when `checkJs` is enabled (or verify `.js` is excluded when `allowJs` is disabled).
